title: Ackermann Geometry and the Turning Circle: The Bicycle Model, the Two Steering Angles of a Car, the Smallest Circle It Can Drive and the Speed It Can Drive It At

questions.question: Why can a car not turn on the spot?
options: The turn rate is the speed times tan(steer) over the wheelbase: no speed, no turn
questions.explanation: Its rear wheels point where it points.

questions.question: The smallest circle of the car was:
questions.explanation: L over tan of the largest angle.

questions.question: At the smallest circle the inner and the outer front wheels differed by:
questions.explanation: They point at right angles to the lines to the centre.

questions.question: The lane a car needs at its smallest circle is:
questions.explanation: The outer front wheel sweeps further out.

questions.question: What sets the fastest speed round a circle on gravel?
questions.explanation: The tyres can give mu g sideways.

questions.question: Why is the Ackermann difference invisible on a big circle?
options: On a large radius the two angles are nearly equal
questions.explanation: On 20 m the difference is under a tenth of a degree.
